name: Cryogenic tensile characterization of hydrogen-system metal or composite at 20 K (NPL method class)
plain_name: Test how a hydrogen-system material stretches and fails near 20 K
description: Test how a hydrogen-system material stretches and fails near 20 K. A bounded, source-grounded procedure profile; compatibility covers the listed checks and does not guarantee measured scientific performance.

sources.citation: National Physical Laboratory: Cryogenic testing services

requirements.rationale: Select the documented20 K mechanical test condition relevant to liquid-hydrogen service. These are this profile's reviewed procedure conditions, not a universal requirement for the scientific field.
Cryogenic grips, a mechanical load path and force/strain measurement are essential. These are this profile's reviewed procedure conditions, not a universal requirement for the scientific field.

missing_information: This is a documented test-method class, not a complete ASTM/ISO test recipe.
Coupon dimensions, load range, strain rate, extensometry and gauge-length temperature uniformity must be agreed with the facility; no strength prediction is made.
confirmation_note: Profile author reviewed these exact sourced conditions on 2026-10-31. The application must still require the user's review/confirmation; all edits invalidate confirmation.
